name: EMA and National Medicines Agencies
description: EMA and National Medicines Agencies control market authorisation, inspections, variations, safety monitoring and withdrawals. The immediate issue is dossier quality, pharmacovigilance, manufacturing compliance and benefit-risk evidence. Its decisions or actions can block approval, narrow labels, require studies or suspend products.
urgency_rationale: Central and national regulatory decisions can change market access across multiple countries.
intel_dossier: 🔎 EMA human medicines regulation: EMA coordinates the centralised authorisation and supervision of human medicines. | https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/human-regulatory-overview
🔎 EMA pharmacovigilance: EMA coordinates safety monitoring with national authorities, patients and healthcare professionals. | https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/pharmacovigilance
🔎 EudraLex: EudraLex is the EU body of pharmaceutical law and supporting guidance. | https://health.ec.europa.eu/medicinal-products/eudralex_en
alternate_rationale: Keep Satisfied may fit a mature low-risk portfolio, but active procedures require continuous working-level engagement.

engagement_tactics.label: Create a single evidence room and joint workplan with EMA and National Medicines Agencies
engagement_tactics.rationale: Gives the authority traceable data, named owners and early visibility of corrective action.

engagement_tactics.label: Rely mainly on trade-association lobbying
engagement_tactics.rationale: Collective advocacy cannot substitute for company-specific compliance evidence.

engagement_tactics.label: Wait for a notice, inspection or deficiency letter
engagement_tactics.rationale: Reactive engagement reduces room to correct problems before enforcement.

name: EU HTA Bodies and National Payers
description: EU HTA Bodies and National Payers assess comparative clinical value and determine reimbursement, price and access conditions. The immediate issue is joint clinical assessment readiness, comparator choice, real-world evidence and budget impact. Its decisions or actions can limit reimbursement, impose managed entry or delay uptake.
urgency_rationale: HTA evidence decisions are time-bound and directly affect launch sequencing.
intel_dossier: 🔎 EU Health Technology Assessment: The HTA Regulation applies through joint clinical assessments and national reimbursement processes. | https://health.ec.europa.eu/health-technology-assessment_en

🔎 EU pharmaceutical legislation reform: The European Commission sets out the reform objectives and implementation direction. | https://health.ec.europa.eu/medicinal-products/reform-eu-pharmaceutical-legislation_en

🔎 EU competition policy for pharmaceuticals: The Commission applies competition and state-aid rules to medicines and health services. | https://competition-policy.ec.europa.eu/sectors/pharmaceuticals-health-services/legislation_en
alternate_rationale: Keep Satisfied is possible after stable reimbursement, but new indications and reassessment require close management.

engagement_tactics.label: Co-develop an evidence, access and supply plan with EU HTA Bodies and National Payers
engagement_tactics.rationale: Links price or procurement discussions to outcomes, affordability and continuity of supply.

engagement_tactics.label: Offer a blanket discount with no access conditions
engagement_tactics.rationale: Sacrifices value without ensuring uptake, adherence or patient access.

engagement_tactics.label: Escalate the negotiation through public criticism
engagement_tactics.rationale: Hardens positions and can damage trust with other payers.

name: European Commission, HERA and Member-State Health Ministries
description: European Commission, HERA and Member-State Health Ministries shape pharmaceutical law, shortage policy, strategic procurement and industrial resilience. The immediate issue is critical-medicine supply, localisation, incentives and obligations under the legislative reform. Its decisions or actions can change exclusivity, procurement preference, reporting duties and manufacturing economics.
urgency_rationale: The reform and resilience agenda affects portfolio and network choices now.
intel_dossier: 🔎 EU pharmaceutical legislation reform: The European Commission sets out the reform objectives and implementation direction. | https://health.ec.europa.eu/medicinal-products/reform-eu-pharmaceutical-legislation_en
🔎 Critical Medicines Act: EU policy focuses on medicine availability, supply resilience and production capacity. | https://health.ec.europa.eu/medicinal-products/critical-medicines-act_en

🔎 EU competition policy for pharmaceuticals: The Commission applies competition and state-aid rules to medicines and health services. | https://competition-policy.ec.europa.eu/sectors/pharmaceuticals-health-services/legislation_en
alternate_rationale: Keep Satisfied applies where the company is a reliable strategic supplier; legislative transition still calls for close management.

engagement_tactics.label: Align investment, resilience and transition milestones with European Commission, HERA and Member-State Health Ministries
engagement_tactics.rationale: Connects business commitments to public-policy outcomes and makes delivery auditable.

engagement_tactics.label: Seek an informal exemption through political contacts
engagement_tactics.rationale: Creates governance and reputational exposure without solving the underlying issue.

engagement_tactics.label: Announce investment before land, technology and economics are validated
engagement_tactics.rationale: Overpromising weakens credibility and can trigger public backlash.

name: European Patient Organisations and EURORDIS Networks
description: European Patient Organisations and EURORDIS Networks bring lived experience into regulatory, HTA and access decisions. The immediate issue is meaningful involvement, transparent evidence, equitable access and shortage communication. Its decisions or actions can influence regulators, HTA bodies, Parliament and public opinion.
urgency_rationale: For rare or severe disease, access and evidence concerns carry immediate legitimacy.
intel_dossier: 🔎 EURORDIS: EURORDIS represents a large network of rare-disease patient organisations. | https://www.eurordis.org/
🔎 EU Health Technology Assessment: The HTA Regulation applies through joint clinical assessments and national reimbursement processes. | https://health.ec.europa.eu/health-technology-assessment_en
🔎 EMA pharmacovigilance: EMA coordinates safety monitoring with national authorities, patients and healthcare professionals. | https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/pharmacovigilance
alternate_rationale: Manage Closely is appropriate for orphan products, contested endpoints or severe access gaps.

engagement_tactics.label: Create a representative forum with independent data review for European Patient Organisations and EURORDIS Networks
engagement_tactics.rationale: Combines voice, verifiable evidence and a public commitments tracker.

engagement_tactics.label: Replace consultation with local donations
engagement_tactics.rationale: Philanthropy does not address rights, exposure or operational impacts.

engagement_tactics.label: Engage only through local political intermediaries
engagement_tactics.rationale: Excludes affected groups and makes consent appear managed rather than earned.

name: Hospitals, Prescribers and Hospital Pharmacists
description: Hospitals, Prescribers and Hospital Pharmacists translate approvals and reimbursement into treatment pathways and medicine use. The immediate issue is clinical utility, formulary evidence, administration burden and dependable supply. Its decisions or actions can restrict use, redesign pathways or accelerate adoption.
urgency_rationale: Shortages and hospital formulary decisions can change demand quickly.
intel_dossier: 🔎 EMA human medicines regulation: EMA coordinates the centralised authorisation and supervision of human medicines. | https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/human-regulatory-overview
🔎 EU Health Technology Assessment: The HTA Regulation applies through joint clinical assessments and national reimbursement processes. | https://health.ec.europa.eu/health-technology-assessment_en
🔎 Critical Medicines Act: EU policy focuses on medicine availability, supply resilience and production capacity. | https://health.ec.europa.eu/medicinal-products/critical-medicines-act_en
alternate_rationale: Keep Informed may suffice for stable primary-care products; specialist launches need close partnership.

engagement_tactics.label: Build a joint service, quality and continuity plan with Hospitals, Prescribers and Hospital Pharmacists
engagement_tactics.rationale: Makes performance expectations explicit and creates early-warning triggers.

engagement_tactics.label: Promise priority supply to every major account
engagement_tactics.rationale: Conflicting commitments become impossible to honour during a disruption.

engagement_tactics.label: Limit contact to sales teams
engagement_tactics.rationale: Commercial dialogue alone misses quality, safety and operational dependencies.

name: European CMOs, API Suppliers and Wholesalers
description: European CMOs, API Suppliers and Wholesalers provide manufacturing capacity, critical inputs, batch release and distribution continuity. The immediate issue is shortage prevention, geographic concentration, GMP compliance and cold-chain resilience. Its decisions or actions can cause EU-wide shortages or regulatory non-compliance.
urgency_rationale: Supply resilience is an explicit EU policy priority and failures spread across borders.
intel_dossier: 🔎 Critical Medicines Act: EU policy focuses on medicine availability, supply resilience and production capacity. | https://health.ec.europa.eu/medicinal-products/critical-medicines-act_en
🔎 EudraLex: EudraLex is the EU body of pharmaceutical law and supporting guidance. | https://health.ec.europa.eu/medicinal-products/eudralex_en
🔎 EMA human medicines regulation: EMA coordinates the centralised authorisation and supervision of human medicines. | https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/human-regulatory-overview
alternate_rationale: Keep Informed fits non-critical components; sole-source or critical medicines require joint control.

engagement_tactics.label: Segment critical suppliers and fund traceability plus remediation with European CMOs, API Suppliers and Wholesalers
engagement_tactics.rationale: Protects continuity while addressing root causes rather than shifting them down-tier.

engagement_tactics.label: Terminate every non-conforming supplier immediately
engagement_tactics.rationale: Abrupt exits can deepen shortages and hide problems in less visible tiers.

engagement_tactics.label: Accept annual self-certification as sufficient
engagement_tactics.rationale: High-risk supply chains require evidence, audit and corrective-action closure.

name: Scientific Staff, Plant Workers and Works Councils
description: Scientific Staff, Plant Workers and Works Councils hold specialised knowledge and formal consultation rights during operational change. The immediate issue is skills, restructuring, automation, safety and research integrity. Its decisions or actions can delay restructuring, lose critical knowledge or expose compliance weaknesses.
urgency_rationale: Works-council timelines and scarce skills make late engagement costly.
intel_dossier: 🔎 EudraLex: EudraLex is the EU body of pharmaceutical law and supporting guidance. | https://health.ec.europa.eu/medicinal-products/eudralex_en

🔎 EU pharmaceutical legislation reform: The European Commission sets out the reform objectives and implementation direction. | https://health.ec.europa.eu/medicinal-products/reform-eu-pharmaceutical-legislation_en
🔎 EMA human medicines regulation: EMA coordinates the centralised authorisation and supervision of human medicines. | https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/human-regulatory-overview
alternate_rationale: Manage Closely applies during site closure, transfer, major automation or collective bargaining.

engagement_tactics.label: Negotiate a safety, skills and workload plan with Scientific Staff, Plant Workers and Works Councils
engagement_tactics.rationale: Uses formal worker voice and measurable actions to reduce operational and labour risk.

engagement_tactics.label: Use attendance bonuses to suppress grievances
engagement_tactics.rationale: Treats symptoms, discourages reporting and can worsen fatigue-related risk.

engagement_tactics.label: Communicate only through line supervisors
engagement_tactics.rationale: Workers need trusted escalation channels and protection from retaliation.

name: Environmental Authorities and Manufacturing Communities
description: Environmental Authorities and Manufacturing Communities scrutinise emissions, antimicrobial releases, water use and local industrial impacts. The immediate issue is permit compliance, pollution prevention and credible environmental performance. Its decisions or actions can constrain sites, litigate permits or intensify public pressure.
urgency_rationale: Environmental concerns are moving from voluntary ESG into operating requirements.

engagement_tactics.rationale: Philanthropy does not address rights, exposure or operational impacts.

engagement_tactics.label: Engage only through local political intermediaries
engagement_tactics.rationale: Excludes affected groups and makes consent appear managed rather than earned.

name: European Investors, Banks and Stewardship Teams
description: European Investors, Banks and Stewardship Teams assess pipeline quality, regulatory transition, pricing and supply resilience. The immediate issue is capital allocation, exclusivity changes, litigation and transition capex. Its decisions or actions can reprice risk, restrict finance or challenge boards.
urgency_rationale: Legislative reform and supply mandates can alter long-term cash flows.
intel_dossier: 🔎 EU pharmaceutical legislation reform: The European Commission sets out the reform objectives and implementation direction. | https://health.ec.europa.eu/medicinal-products/reform-eu-pharmaceutical-legislation_en
🔎 Critical Medicines Act: EU policy focuses on medicine availability, supply resilience and production capacity. | https://health.ec.europa.eu/medicinal-products/critical-medicines-act_en

engagement_tactics.label: Brief European Investors, Banks and Stewardship Teams on material risks, capital needs, milestones and downside cases
engagement_tactics.rationale: Allows investors to test execution quality rather than rely on broad commitments.

engagement_tactics.label: Describe the exposure as immaterial until a charge is booked
engagement_tactics.rationale: Delayed disclosure increases surprise and credibility risk.

engagement_tactics.label: Promise a fixed outcome that management cannot control
engagement_tactics.rationale: Overconfidence creates litigation and trust risk if regulation or markets change.

name: Competition, Data-Protection and Research-Ethics Authorities

urgency_rationale: Exposure rises rapidly when digital health, AI or market concentration is central to strategy.
